description: Designing systems that collect and use personal data without exposing people, from threat modelling and anonymisation to differential privacy, anonymous communication, secure computation and private machine learning. In the lab students implement the techniques, attack them, and measure what privacy they actually deliver.
modelledOn: Dwork and Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Hoepman, Privacy Is Hard and Seven Other Myths (privacy design strategies)
Deng et al., a privacy threat analysis framework (LINDDUN)
Evans, Kolesnikov and Rosulek, A Pragmatic Introduction to Secure Multi-Party Computation
outcomes: Model privacy threats in a system using data flow diagrams, adversary models and a structured threat taxonomy.
Measure re-identification risk and apply k-anonymity and its refinements, and demonstrate their weaknesses.
Implement differential privacy mechanisms, track a privacy budget and explain the privacy-utility trade-off.
Explain and simulate anonymous communication, secret-sharing based computation and private set intersection.
Train models with federated learning and differential privacy, and attack them with membership inference.
Audit and compare privacy guarantees and choose a technology for a given use case with reasons.

units.title: Privacy concepts, law and identifiability
topics: Privacy as contextual integrity and informational self-determination; taxonomy of privacy harms
Legal frameworks: Ghana's Data Protection Act, comparable African laws and the GDPR; lawful bases and data subject rights
Principles: purpose limitation, data minimisation, storage limitation and privacy by design
Direct and quasi-identifiers, linkage attacks and re-identification
Data protection impact assessments

units.title: Privacy threat modelling
topics: LINDDUN threat categories: linkability, identifiability, detectability, disclosure, unawareness and non-compliance
Data flow diagrams, trust boundaries and adversary models (honest-but-curious, malicious, global passive)
Privacy risk assessment: likelihood, impact and prioritisation
Privacy design strategies and patterns: minimise, hide, separate, aggregate, inform, control
Worked threat model of a mobile-money or health application

units.title: Anonymisation and privacy-preserving data release
topics: k-anonymity, l-diversity and t-closeness; generalisation, suppression and Mondrian partitioning
Attacks on anonymised data: homogeneity, background knowledge and composition
Pseudonymisation, tokenisation and the pitfalls of hashing identifiers
Synthetic data: generation methods and privacy leakage
Releasing statistics: cell suppression, query auditing and reconstruction attacks
Data sharing agreements, data trusts and secure research enclaves

units.title: Differential privacy
topics: Definition: epsilon and delta, neighbouring datasets, sensitivity, post-processing and composition
Mechanisms: randomised response, Laplace, Gaussian and exponential mechanisms
Privacy budget accounting: basic and advanced composition, zero-concentrated and Renyi accounting
Local versus central models; frequency estimation under local privacy and the shuffle model
Differentially private learning: per-example clipping, noise multiplier and DP-SGD
Deployment practice: choosing epsilon, census and telemetry examples, and open-source libraries

units.title: Anonymous communication
topics: Identifiers and metadata at the network layer; anonymity sets and entropy metrics
Mix networks, onion routing and hidden services; circuit construction
Crowds, DC-nets and message batching
Attacks: traffic correlation, website fingerprinting, intersection and Sybil attacks
Blind signatures, anonymous credentials and private information retrieval

units.title: Secure multi-party computation basics
topics: Adversary models: semi-honest and malicious; ideal functionality and simulation
Secret sharing: additive and polynomial sharing; secure addition and multiplication with Beaver triples
Garbled circuits and oblivious transfer
Private set intersection and homomorphic encryption (Paillier and the idea of BFV and CKKS)
Trusted execution environments and confidential computing: assumptions and costs
Applications: cross-bank fraud analytics, private statistics and salary studies

units.title: Federated learning and privacy
topics: Federated averaging, client sampling, non-identical data and communication cost
Attacks: gradient inversion, membership inference, model inversion and memorisation
Secure aggregation and differentially private federated learning
Machine unlearning and the right to erasure
Cross-device learning on phones with low connectivity and cross-silo learning among hospitals
Fairness versus privacy trade-offs

units.title: Evaluating privacy guarantees
topics: Empirical privacy audits: membership inference, shadow models and auditing differential privacy
Risk and utility metrics: prosecutor and journalist risk, information loss and the privacy-utility frontier
Comparing guarantees: syntactic versus semantic privacy, assumptions and threat-model mapping
Implementation pitfalls: floating-point attacks on noise samplers and budget leaks
Red-teaming, bug bounties and certification of privacy claims
Transparency documents: privacy notices, model cards and impact reports

units.title: Privacy engineering in practice
topics: The privacy engineering lifecycle from requirements to operations
Choosing a privacy-enhancing technology: a decision guide by data location, trust and accuracy needs
Cost, performance and governance of deploying privacy-enhancing technologies
Project: privacy architecture for a health or payments data product

schedule.title: Privacy concepts, law and re-identification
schedule.exercise: Show with a linkage experiment that quasi-identifiers re-identify people, classify ten processing activities by lawful basis, and outline a DPIA.

tasks.title: Link a provided anonymised health table to a public list by postcode, birth year and sex, and count how many records are uniquely re-identified
Classify ten data processing activities by lawful basis, purpose and data subject right in a scenario, and flag two that break purpose limitation
Run a data protection impact assessment for a mobile-money credit scoring pilot in a scenario, listing data flows, risks, necessity tests and mitigations

schedule.title: Threat modelling for privacy
schedule.exercise: Draw a data flow diagram of a school-fees app, apply LINDDUN to it, and rank the top three threats with design strategies to address them.

tasks.title: Draw a data flow diagram of a school-fees payment app with trust boundaries, and label each flow with the personal data it carries
Apply LINDDUN to a ride-hailing app in a scenario, listing at least one threat in each category with a concrete example
Threat-model a mobile-money app against honest-but-curious operator and global passive observer adversaries, rank threats by risk, and choose strategies for the top three

schedule.title: k-anonymity and its failures
schedule.exercise: Anonymise a table to k = 5, attack it with background knowledge, and show why hashed phone numbers are not anonymous.

tasks.title: Compute k-anonymity and l-diversity of a 1,000-row table, then generalise age bands and postcodes until k is 5 and report the suppressed rows
Mount a homogeneity and a background-knowledge attack on a 5-anonymous table and show which sensitive values an attacker can infer for named people
Reverse unsalted hashed phone numbers by brute force, then compare keyed hashing and tokenisation on the same number space

schedule.title: Synthetic data, statistics release and sharing
schedule.exercise: Release a table of counts safely, test whether synthetic data leaks membership, and list the clauses a data sharing agreement needs.

tasks.title: Release a table of counts with small cells suppressed, then recover a suppressed cell from row and column totals to see why suppression alone fails
Draft the key clauses of a data sharing agreement for a research partnership in a scenario covering purpose, retention, onward transfer and breach notice
Generate synthetic data from the marginals of a patient table, then run a membership inference test to measure whether training records are detectably closer
Reconstruct a hidden binary column from 200 noisy subset-sum queries using least squares, and report how noise size changes accuracy

schedule.title: Differential privacy: definitions and mechanisms
schedule.exercise: Prove the Laplace mechanism satisfies epsilon-differential privacy, run randomised response on a sensitive survey, and track a budget over repeated queries.

tasks.title: Apply randomised response to a sensitive survey of 2,000 simulated people, estimate the true proportion, and plot error against the coin probability
Implement the Laplace mechanism for counts and means with clipping, and check empirically that outputs on neighbouring datasets differ by at most e^epsilon
Track a privacy budget over 20 repeated queries using basic composition and zero-concentrated accounting, and show how many more queries the tighter accounting allows

schedule.title: Local privacy, private learning and deployment
schedule.exercise: Estimate app-category frequencies under local privacy, train a model with clipped noisy gradients, and justify an epsilon for a mobility data release.

tasks.title: Simulate local differential privacy with unary encoding for 10 app categories, aggregate reports from 10,000 users, and compare estimated with true frequencies
Train a logistic regression with per-example gradient clipping and Gaussian noise in the style of DP-SGD, and chart accuracy against epsilon from 0.5 to 8
Choose epsilon, granularity and neighbouring definition for releasing weekly mobility counts to a ministry in a scenario, and defend the utility-privacy trade-off

schedule.title: Anonymity networks and their attacks
schedule.exercise: Compute the entropy of an anonymity set, simulate a mix network, and explain how an observer who sees both ends of an onion circuit can link its users.

tasks.title: Compute anonymity set sizes and entropy for a user population described by browser attributes, and find which attribute reduces anonymity the most
Simulate a three-hop mix network with batching and random delay, and measure how the batch threshold changes sender-receiver linkability
Issue and verify a blind RSA signature on a token with toy keys, and show the signer cannot link it to the issuing session
Run a correlation attack on simulated traffic traces entering and leaving an onion-routing network, and measure its accuracy as padding and noise increase

schedule.title: Secure multi-party computation
schedule.exercise: Sum private salaries with additive secret sharing, evaluate a garbled AND gate, and compare MPC, homomorphic encryption and a trusted enclave for joint fraud detection.

tasks.title: Split three private salaries into additive shares among three parties, compute their sum without revealing any single value, and verify the result
Implement 1-out-of-2 oblivious transfer with toy parameters and use it to evaluate a garbled AND gate, checking all four input cases
Compute a private set intersection of two hospitals' patient identifier lists with a Diffie-Hellman based protocol, and compare its cost with plain hashing
Evaluate whether banks should use MPC, homomorphic encryption or a trusted enclave for joint fraud detection, comparing trust assumptions, cost and regulation

schedule.title: Federated learning and its attacks
schedule.exercise: Compare federated and central training on skewed data, run a membership inference attack, and show how secure aggregation hides individual updates.

tasks.title: Simulate federated averaging across 10 clients with identical and skewed local data, and compare global accuracy after 20 rounds with central training
Run a loss-threshold membership inference attack on a small overfit classifier, and report attack accuracy before and after regularisation
Implement pairwise-mask secure aggregation for five clients, show the server sees only masked updates, and handle one client dropping out

schedule.title: Unlearning, deployment and fairness
schedule.exercise: Decide how to honour an erasure request for training data, plan a federated round for phones on slow networks, and measure who bears the accuracy cost of privacy.

tasks.title: Handle an erasure request in a scenario where a person's data trained a deployed model, and decide between deletion, retraining and approximate unlearning
Measure accuracy for majority and minority subgroups as DP noise increases in a trained classifier, and plot the gap to see who pays for privacy
Design a cross-device federated round for phones on slow networks with 30 percent dropout, choosing client fraction, rounds and compression, and simulate the result

schedule.title: Measuring and comparing privacy
schedule.exercise: Audit a claimed epsilon empirically, plot risk against information loss for three generalisation levels, and recommend a technology for a ministry data-sharing proposal.

tasks.title: Compute prosecutor and journalist re-identification risk for a table, add an information-loss measure, and plot risk against loss for three generalisation levels
Audit a differentially private counting mechanism by running it on neighbouring datasets, estimating privacy loss from a million samples, and checking the claimed epsilon
Compare k-anonymity, differential privacy and secure computation for a ministry data-sharing proposal in a scenario, map each to its threat model, and recommend one with caveats

schedule.title: Implementation pitfalls, red teams and transparency
schedule.exercise: Exploit a flawed noise sampler, red-team a privacy-preserving release within a query budget, and write a plain-language privacy notice and model card.

tasks.title: Write a plain-language privacy notice and a one-page model card for a prediction service, then check them against a list of transparency requirements
Exploit floating-point rounding in a naive Laplace sampler to distinguish neighbouring datasets, then fix it with a discrete mechanism
Red-team a provided privacy-preserving release by attempting linkage, reconstruction and membership attacks within a query budget, and write a findings report with severity ratings

schedule.title: Choosing and deploying privacy technologies
schedule.exercise: Choose a technology for five use cases with a decision guide, cost the options, and present a privacy architecture for a national health data platform.

tasks.title: Pick a privacy-enhancing technology for five use cases in a scenario using a decision guide on data location, trust and accuracy needs
Estimate runtime, bandwidth and accuracy cost of secure aggregation, DP noise and a trusted enclave for a one-million-user analytics job from supplied benchmarks
Present a privacy architecture for a national health data platform to a mock review board, defend the threat model, technology choices and residual risks, and revise after objections
